answer: Like a grove where every tree must earn its place in the soil, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade. A single identity costs little, but a Sybil attacker must fund thousands of stakes at once, and any proven fraud burns the stake like a hollow wind through dry leaves — the loss scales with the attack. Honest agents keep their deposit and gain reputation, so flooding the network with fake identities becomes a slow, expensive zephyr of a strategy that never pays for itself.
